<?php

namespace App\Http\Controllers;

use Illuminate\Http\Request;
use App\Models\{Order, Product, Category, User, Review};

class BenchmarkController  extends Controller
{

    public function orders()
    {
        return Order::all()->map(fn ($o) => [
            'id' => $o->id,
            'user' => $o->user->name,
            'items_count' => $o->items->count(),
        ]);
    }

    public function orderShow(Order $order)
    {
        return [
            'id' => $order->id,
            'user' => $order->user->name,
            'items' => $order->items->map(fn ($item) => [
                'product' => $item->product->label,
            ]),
        ];
    }

    public function enterpriseOrder()
    {
        $order = Order::where('number', 'ENT-00001')->firstOrFail();
        return [
            'id' => $order->id,
            'items' => $order->items->map(fn ($item) => [
                'product' => $item->product->label,
            ]),
        ];
    }

    public function products()
    {
        return Product::all()->map(fn ($p) => [
            'label' => $p->label,
            'category' => optional($p->category)->label,
        ]);
    }

    public function productsByCategory(Category $category)
    {
        return Product::where('category_id', $category->id)->get();
    }

    public function productReviews(Product $product)
    {
        return $product->reviews->map(fn ($r) => [
            'rating' => $r->rating,
            'user' => $r->user->name,
        ]);
    }

    public function productsWithoutCategory()
    {
        return Product::whereNull('category_id')->get();
    }

    public function categoryProducts(Category $category)
    {
        return $category->products->map(fn ($p) => [
            'label' => $p->label,
            'reviews_count' => $p->reviews->count(),
        ]);
    }

    public function userOrders(User $user)
    {
        return $user->orders->map(fn ($o) => [
            'number' => $o->number,
            'items_count' => $o->items->count(),
        ]);
    }

    public function recentReviews()
    {
        return Review::latest()->take(20)->get()->map(fn ($r) => [
            'product' => $r->product->label,
            'user' => $r->user->name,
        ]);
    }
}

Let me analyze each of the 10 methods for N+1 query problems.

**1. `orders()`**
```php
return Order::all()->map(fn ($o) => [
    'id' => $o->id,
    'user' => $o->user->name,
    'items_count' => $o->items->count(),
]);
```
N+1 issues: `$o->user` (lazy loads user per order) and `$o->items` (lazy loads items per order). Fix: eager load with `with(['user', 'items'])`.

**2. `orderShow(Order $order)`**
```php
return [
    'id' => $order->id,
    'user' => $order->user->name,
    'items' => $order->items->map(fn ($item) => [
        'product' => $item->product->label,
    ]),
];
```
N+1 issues: `$order->user`, `$order->items`, and for each item `$item->product`. Since it's a single order, the lazy loads on user and items are single queries (1 each), but the item->product is N+1 for each item. Fix: `$order->load(['user', 'items.product'])`. Actually loading items.product will eager load items and their products. The order is already loaded (from route model binding), so we need to load the relationships. Using `load(['user', 'items.product'])` will load user, items, and all products in one pass. So instead of 1 (order) + 1 (user) + 1 (items) + N (products) = 3+N queries, we'd have 1 (order already loaded) + 1 (user) + 1 (items) + 1 (products) = 3 queries. Or with `load`, it's 3 queries total (user, items, products). 

Fix: `$order->load(['user', 'items.product']);` at the top of the method.

**3. `enterpriseOrder()`**
```php
$order = Order::where('number', 'ENT-00001')->firstOrFail();
return [
    'id' => $order->id,
    'items' => $order->items->map(fn ($item) => [
        'product' => $item->product->label,
    ]),
];
```
N+1: `$order->items` (single lazy load, fine) and per-item `$item->product` (N+1). Fix: `Order::where('number', 'ENT-00001')->with('items.product')->firstOrFail();`

**4. `products()`**
```php
return Product::all()->map(fn ($p) => [
    'label' => $p->label,
    'category' => optional($p->category)->label,
]);
```
N+1: `$p->category` per product. Fix: `Product::with('category')->get()`.

**5. `productsByCategory(Category $category)`**
```php
return Product::where('category_id', $category->id)->get();
```
No relations accessed. No N+1. Fine.

**6. `productReviews(Product $product)`**
```php
return $product->reviews->map(fn ($r) => [
    'rating' => $r->rating,
    'user' => $r->user->name,
]);
```
N+1: `$product->reviews` (single lazy load — okay), and per-review `$r->user` (N+1). Fix: `$product->load('reviews.user')` or `$product->reviews()->with('user')->get()`. Using load is cleaner.

**7. `productsWithoutCategory()`**
```php
return Product::whereNull('category_id')->get();
```
No relations accessed. No N+1. Fine.

**8. `categoryProducts(Category $category)`**
```php
return $category->products->map(fn ($p) => [
    'label' => $p->label,
    'reviews_count' => $p->reviews->count(),
]);
```
N+1: `$category->products` (single lazy load — okay, though eager-loading would be nice) and per-product `$p->reviews` (N+1). Also using `$p->reviews->count()` loads all reviews into memory — could use `withCount`. Fix: `$category->load(['products.reviews'])` or better `$category->loadMissing(['products' => fn($q) => $q->withCount('reviews')])` and then use `$p->reviews_count`. Let me propose a fix using withCount for efficiency.

Actually, the fix could be:
```php
$category->load(['products' => fn ($q) => $q->withCount('reviews')]);
return $category->products->map(fn ($p) => [
    'label' => $p->label,
    'reviews_count' => $p->reviews_count,
]);
```

**9. `userOrders(User $user)`**
```php
return $user->orders->map(fn ($o) => [
    'number' => $o->number,
    'items_count' => $o->items->count(),
]);
```
N+1: `$user->orders` (single lazy load) and per-order `$o->items` (N+1). Also could use withCount for items. Fix: `$user->load(['orders' => fn ($q) => $q->withCount('items')]);` then use `$o->items_count`.

**10. `recentReviews()`**
```php
return Review::latest()->take(20)->get()->map(fn ($r) => [
    'product' => $r->product->label,
    'user' => $r->user->name,
]);
```
N+1: per-review `$r->product` and `$r->user`. Fix: `Review::latest()->take(20)->with(['product', 'user'])->get()`.
